products.processing: Key processing and packaging in Québec under this certification.

products.name: Balanced Espresso Coffee Beans
products.summary: The listing identifies Laval as the roasting location for this 1 kg coffee. Its certification describes where it was processed.

products.summary: The Buy BC product entry identifies the Okanagan as the growing region for the Salish apples in this juice.
products.inputs: The producer’s description identifies 100% B.C.-grown Salish apples from the Okanagan.

products.name: Cold Pressed Blueberry Lemonade
products.summary: The listing identifies an Abbotsford cold-pressed juice manufacturer and names blueberry, lemon, filtered water and simple syrup.
products.inputs: The listing names four ingredients. It gives no growing location for the berries or lemons.
products.processing: The program lists Chasers Fresh Juice as a cold-pressed juice manufacturer in Abbotsford, B.C.

products.name: Maple Syrup Leaf Bottle
products.summary: The 100 mL leaf bottle belongs to Acadian Maple’s pure syrup range. A separate maker statement traces that syrup to harvesters in Nova Scotia.
products.inputs: Maple syrup sourced from the sugar woods of Nova Scotia.
products.processing: Acadian Maple describes its role processing Nova Scotia syrup. The bottle listing gives no plant address.
products.ownership: Acadian Maple identifies Authentic Seacoast Company as its acquirer in 2019. This is dated company history.

products.name: Steel Cut Oat Blend Porridge Oats
products.summary: Rogers prints the federal food-origin wording on this blend. Its company page identifies mills in Armstrong and Chilliwack, B.C.

products.processing: The maker identifies B.C. mills. The product page does not assign this blend to a particular mill.

products.name: Hockey Sticks
products.summary: Ontario Made lists Roustan’s hockey sticks for teams, retailers and selected brands. The listing covers a product family and supplies no model or barcode.
products.processing: Ontario Made eligibility requires the registered product’s last substantial transformation to take place in Ontario.

products.name: Hockey Scoreboard
products.summary: Harris Time is named on the program entry for this scoreboard. The entry supplies no model number or origin for its electronics.
products.processing: Last substantial manufacturing transformation in Ontario under the program’s criteria.

products.name: Low-Angle Block Plane
products.summary: Lee Valley displays this wording beside the named Veritas hand plane. The product page does not disclose the share of Canadian production costs.
products.processing: The product page identifies Canada. It gives no factory location or imported-parts qualifier beside the displayed claim.
products.ownership: Lee Valley describes its business as family-owned and Canadian. This company statement is a separate source from the country wording on the plane.

rules.name: Aliments du Québec
rules.description: At least 85% of ingredients originate in Québec. All main ingredients must come from Québec. Key processing and packaging take place in the province.

rules.name: Aliments préparés au Québec
rules.description: The product is entirely processed in Québec. Ingredients may come from Québec or elsewhere.

rules.name: Buy BC
rules.description: Eligibility covers products wholly grown, raised or caught in B.C., or products processed and packaged there with at least 51% of direct production costs originating in B.C. The product listing may provide more specific evidence.

rules.name: Ontario Made
rules.description: The program registers products whose final substantial manufacturing transformation took place in Ontario. It allows imported components. Registration applies to the listed products.

rules.name: Product of Canada · food
rules.description: CFIA describes this claim as requiring Canadian processing and labour and Canadian origin for all significant ingredients. Minor imported ingredients can qualify for exceptions.

rules.name: Made in Canada · food
rules.description: CFIA looks for the final substantial transformation in Canada and a qualifier indicating whether the ingredients are imported or both domestic and imported.

rules.name: Product of Canada · non-food
rules.description: The Competition Bureau’s guidance considers final substantial transformation in Canada and at least 98% of direct production or manufacturing costs incurred here.

rules.name: Made in Canada · non-food
rules.description: The Competition Bureau’s guidance considers final substantial transformation in Canada, at least 51% of direct production costs incurred here and an appropriate qualifier for the claim. A manufacturer’s label alone does not disclose its cost calculation.

rules.name: Producer location statement
rules.description: Read the maker’s exact product and place wording. Geographic details about one ingredient, a process or a range apply only to the scope stated.
